item.title: Just 21 and American, IShowSpeed Shows How to Market Africa Tourism
item.description: Popular creators such as IShowSpeed can help reshape Africa’s global image faster than tourism campaigns.

item.title: What If OTAs Are the Wrong Signal on Travel Demand?
item.description: The demand story has become messier, and OTAs might just be good at capturing the demand that exists.

item.title: 7 Travel Claims — Fact or Fiction?
item.description: The data shows the travel industry may be overestimating some strengths — and underestimating certain risks.

item.title: 4 European Countries Issue Travel Advisories for Minneapolis
item.description: The unrest and large-scale protests in Minneapolis drew the attention of several foreign governments, which urged their citizens to remain alert when traveling to the U.S.

item.title: Southwest Expects Boost From Bag Fees, Assigned Seating
item.description: Southwest is forecasting a profitable 2026 after ripping up its business model to implement assigned seating and baggage fees.

item.title: Smart Glasses to AI Agents: 4 Shifts for Travel From Meta’s Earnings
item.description: Meta highlighted key AI developments on its fourth-quarter 2025 earnings call in consumer, retail and developer terms. But there are obvious travel applications too, and they could solve some of the industry's toughest challenges.

item.title: India-EU Free Trade Deal and the Travel Impact as Visa Reforms Move Forward
item.description: Europe has been among India's dream destination for a long time, but visa woes have been the biggest obstacles. The FTA now lays ground for processes that could now allow EU to fully unlock India's tourism potential.

item.title: Wizz Air Shuts Down U.S. Route Talk, Keeps World Cup Charters in Play
item.description: Wizz Air’s U.S. filing looked like the opening whistle on a transatlantic push, but management says it was just a paperwork technicality. However, World Cup charters could still come off the bench.

item.title: Indian Hotels Company’s Boutique Acquisition: Brij Hospitality’s Next Move
item.description: IHCL is acquiring smaller chains to make the most of the hospitality boom in India. But it does not seem interested in overhauling how these chains actually operate as long as their models work.

item.title: IndiGo CEO Bets on ‘Fit-For-Purpose Flying’ and Explains What Went Wrong in December
item.description: IndiGo wants to grow beyond its low-cost roots without losing price-sensitive flyers. But, December showed that growth and resilience don’t always move together. What and how it fixes next will matter.
